business_problem: OTTO's on-premises Kafka setup and custom partner integrations could not keep up with marketplace growth, making product data hard to share quickly with new teams and partners while consuming too much of a small platform team's time.
solution_summary: OTTO adopted Confluent Cloud as the foundation of a new event exchange platform for its marketplace systems after self-managing Apache Kafka on premises became too operationally expensive. The team now uses the managed streaming platform as the core distribution layer for product data, while OTTO-built microservices pull the relevant information, validate it, process it, and create new streams for downstream consumers. Instead of writing a custom integration for every new partner or client, OTTO standardized on a single protocol over Kafka and Confluent so teams can access product data much faster. That architecture modernized a decade-old data estate, removed monolithic product-data bottlenecks, and gave engineers room to focus on platform capabilities rather than Kafka maintenance.

solution_components.name: Confluent Cloud
solution_components.role: Provides the managed event exchange platform OTTO uses to distribute validated product data to downstream consumers.

data_flow: OTTO microservices pull product data from source systems, validate and process it, publish new streams through Confluent Cloud, and make the resulting data available to partner and client systems over one shared Kafka-based protocol.
business_outcome: OTTO reduced operational burden, accelerated onboarding for data consumers, and improved product-data freshness so marketplace partners can act on current information much faster.
architecture_clues: OTTO's microservices pull, validate, and republish product data as streams.
The event exchange platform replaced separate partner-specific implementations with one protocol.
The modernization effort targets a decade-old core data infrastructure.
